name: Auckland University of Technology
summary: Three Auckland campuses and 250+ programmes; 89% of bachelor's students complete workplace experience as part of their degree.
noDeadline: Apply at least three months before the programme starts

ib.text: International Baccalaureate with successful completion of a minimum of 24 points meets the bachelor's entry requirement; some programmes ask more or add a portfolio, interview or English test.

apply.via: AUT online application (Arion) or an AUT agent

programmes.name: Bachelor of International Hospitality Management
programmes.about: A three-year, 360-point degree on how hospitality businesses run: food and beverage, accommodation, human resources, strategy and marketing, ending with workplace experience on a project with an organisation.
programmes.selectionNote: Entry follows the general international rule, IB with 24 points; no portfolio or interview is listed. Starts 22 February or 12 July 2027.

flagshipSource.title: AUT research strengths: sport science, public health, biomedical technology, and tourism and hospitality

programmes.name: Bachelor of Sport, Exercise and Health
programmes.credential: Bachelor of Sport, Exercise and Health
programmes.about: A flexible 360-point degree on sport, movement, leadership, physical education, health and exercise science, with workplace experience at an industry partner and room to combine sport with other subjects such as journalism.
programmes.selectionNote: Entry follows the general international rule, IB with 24 points. Starts 22 February or 12 July 2027 on the North and South campuses.

flagshipSource.title: AUT research strengths: sport science, public health, biomedical technology, and tourism and hospitality

notes: EU citizens pay the international fee, which AUT says reflects the full cost of tuition: for 2027 about NZ$38,360 for a Bachelor of Arts and NZ$51,360 for Engineering (Honours), including the student services levy.
You can apply for up to five programmes, in order of preference; AUT processes your first preference first.
Most undergraduate programmes start in both Semester 1 (February) and Semester 2 (July); a few start only at the beginning of the year.
